newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: FRASER & NEAVE SLUMPS TO 54-MONTH LOW.
newsitem.headline: FRASER & NEAVE SLUMPS TO 54-MONTH LOW.

text.p: Soft drinks conglomerate Fraser & Neave Ltd shares slumped to a 54-month low of Singapore $8.90 on Wednesday.
At 0720 GMT, the stock was changing hands at S$8.95, down 60 cents. Volume was a moderately active 553,000 units.
Analysts said the stock was being sold down on the back of a sell recommendation report by Jardine Fleming Securities analyst Simon Roger.
"I can't think of any fresh news that would trigger the selling," said an analyst with a European firm.
A Jardine spokeswoman said the report would have to be distributed to Jardine clients first before being made public.
Analysts from other stockbroking firms in Singapore said the report was making an impact as Roger is a rated conglomerate analyst with a following among fund managers.
"But most houses have a sell on the company already because of a sharp drop in earnings as their property profits dry up," said one analyst.
Singapore food companies, previously seen as defensive stocks and given high ratings, are going through a derating process.
"A lot of them have regional operations and there is a lot of risks associated with doing business in these countries. So the high ratings cannot be justified," one analyst said.
The F&N group has operations in countries like Malaysia, Vietnam and China.
Another food based company Cerebos Pacific, which makes Brands chicken essence, has also fallen sharply on back of its large exposure to Thailand.
Cerebos was changing hands at S$5.20, up 10 cents from its year low of S$5.10.
